qgrand-model-limitations-noiseless-every: Section I-B, p.3: the authors say 'our model has some limitations' and name all-to-all connectivity, noiseless encoding, noiseless syndrome extraction and noiseless gates. Section VIII repeats it.
qgrand-contributions-stated: Section I-B, p.3: the authors list their own main contributions in these words. It is their own statement of scope. 'For the first time' is their stated claim of what the approach enables.
qgrand-error-rate-definition: Section I-C, p.4: the paper defines how it uses 'error rate' (as bit error rate, after discretization).
qgrand-stabilizer-syndrome-one-bit-per-s: Section IV, p.5, equations (5) to (7): the paper works the controlled-stabilizer circuit through and concludes from commute or anticommute that each stabilizer gives 1 bit; s stabilizers give an s-bit syndrome. The derivation is in the paper.
qgrand-qrlc-construction-c2-clifford: Section V, p.5 to p.6: the paper's own construction (random two-qubit Cliffords from C2, 11 520 elements, applied to random pairs, all-to-all connectivity assumed and used in this work). The link to [45] is stated as the source of the method, not as a result.
qgrand-bernoulli-noise-model-setup: Section V-B1, p.7: the paper states the Bernoulli depolarizing i.i.d. noise model it uses as its example.
qgrand-four-step-framework-definition: Section VI, p.8 to p.9: the paper defines QGRAND for stabilizer codes as these four steps.
qgrand-iteration-physical-correction-cos: Section VI-A, p.9: the paper itself names the 'downside of this approach': physical correction and syndrome extraction at each iteration, which add error. A limit of its own method.
qgrand-bler-underestimates-low-k-limit: Section VII, p.12: the authors state 'by computing the BLER, our results slightly underestimate the codes' performance for very low values of k'. A limit on their own results. Its true type is measured.
qgrand-simulation-setup-qiskit-samples: Section VII, p.12: the paper states its semi-analytical setup (Qiskit, 31 samples per k at least 90 for n = 128, all k for n = 32, 2000 gates for n = 32, patterns up to weight t, N = Bt).
qgrand-open-problem-imperfect-measuremen: Section VIII, p.13: the authors say their model leaves out errors in encoding, decoding and syndrome measurement, and name imperfect measurement as the first step to assess.
qgrand-channel-errors-only: Section VIII, p.12 to p.13: the paper states 'a system model with channel errors only' and that QECCs are considered mostly for communication and memory, not errors during encoding and decoding.
qgrand-fault-tolerance-open: Section VIII, p.13: the authors state that limited connectivity and fault-tolerant systems are 'the subject of ongoing work', so left open.
cum-scope-methods-and-problem: Abstract, p.1: the paper states the methods it explores (QAOA, VQE, quantum annealing; X, XY and 3XY mixers) on the facilities location problem.
cum-objectives-stated: Section I B, p.4 to p.5: the paper lists its own objectives in these words.
cum-quantum-inspired-not-studied: Section I B, p.5: 'We have not looked at the potential of quantum inspired approaches'. The Digital Annealer example is in the same passage.
cum-problem-simplified-grid: Section II B, p.6: 'we will focus solely on optimal ambulance location framed in a simplified operational landscape ... small number of ambulances within a grid ... minimise the aggregate journey time'.
cum-classical-baseline-setup: Section III and Table I caption, p.6 to p.7: Simulated annealing and Tabu from D-Wave Ocean, 2 ambulances on an n x n grid, squared Euclidean distance, 10,000 runs, best reported.
cum-regular-graph-symmetry: Section V C, p.13: the paper states its own setup (regular graph, line or 2D array, undirected edges). The symmetry remark is the authors' stated reason for the choice.
cum-constraints-penalty-or-built-in: Section V D, p.13: the three constraints and the two ways of encoding them are the paper's own statement of its formulation.
cum-dicke-state-gate-cost: Section V D, p.14: the authors state the drawback of the Dicke state approach ('many gate operations ... a major disadvantage') and that they test it only on a simulator at small scale.
cum-five-problem-variants: Section VI A, p.14: the paper specifies 5 small-scale variants; B needs 2 x 2 x 4 = 16 qubits; A, C and D need 5, 8 and 17 qubits.
cum-qaoa-run-setup-figs-3-5: Captions of Figures 3 to 5, p.16 to p.18: 100 random angles, p = 1, 3, 5, Problem A, Nelder-Mead, 2 standard deviation error bars.
cum-figures-of-merit: Section VI B 3, p.17 to p.18: the paper defines the approximation ratio (22), the lowest-state probability, Pr_feas and the number of quantum computer calls, and says the probabilities are computable because it simulates.
cum-mixer-comparison-setup: Section VI B 4, Table IV and Figure 6, p.19 to p.20: the paper states the 3 XY combinations against the X mixer, problems A and C, p = 3 and 5, mean of 100 random-angle runs.
cum-optimiser-no-thorough-review: Section VI B 5, p.21: 'We do not here undertake a thorough review of the optimiser performance and suitability'.
cum-increasing-p-seed-and-strategies: Section VI C 1, p.21 to p.22: the paper defines the seed procedure and the INTERP, EXTRAP1 and EXTRAP2 strategies (INTERP detail in Appendix A 3).
cum-three-xy-mixer-encoding-problem-b: Section VI C 2, Figure 9, p.24 to p.25: the paper describes this encoding for variant B (16 qubits, three ring XY mixers with Hamming weights 1, 1 and 4, penalty term).
cum-3xy-encoding-allows-same-start: Section VI C 2, p.25: the authors state that the encoding does not prevent both ambulances starting at one location and does not guarantee feasible states.
cum-3xy-angle-counts-and-runs: Section VI C 2 and Table VI, p.25 to p.26: the four {beta, gamma} schemes, Nelder-Mead, at least 200 random-angle runs.
cum-vqe-scope-problems-a-b: Section VI E, p.30: the paper states VQE is run only on problems A and B and why. Note: the list of three structures in the text (no initial layer with 1 or 2 entangling layers) differs from the Figure 13 caption (rotation layer plus 2 or 1 entangling layers, or 1 entangling layer only). The value follows the text as quoted.
cum-vqe-circuit-parameter-counts: Figure 13 caption, p.32: the three circuits and their parameter counts (21, 13, 8) are the paper's own statement. The count works for 5 qubits. It differs from the structure list in Section VI E 1 (see cum-vqe-scope-problems-a-b); the caption is the paper's stated setup for Problem A.
cum-vqe-problem-a-table8-setup: Table VIII caption, p.32: means of 100 random-start runs, 2 standard deviations of the mean, L-BFGS-B or SPSA, full wavefunction, 9,000 shots for all-qubit and causal-cone sampling.
cum-qpu-hardware-and-setup: Section VI F 1, p.38: IBM Perth (7 qubits) and Guadalupe (16 qubits), quantum volume 32 each, problems A and B, VQE, limited runs due to scarce QPU time.
cum-annealing-runs-live-hardware: Section VII, p.43: the paper states all annealing runs are on real D-Wave hardware (2000Q and Advantage), gate runs other than VI F are on a noiseless simulator, and comparisons need care.
cum-annealing-penalty-two-constraints: Section VII B 1, equations (25) to (27), p.45: the paper's own cost function; the penalty term captures the 2 constraints. G to J are stated to have a similar form.
cum-annealing-parameter-study-setup-g: Section VII C 1, p.48: problem G on D-Wave Advantage 4.1 (Pegasus), chosen so that parameter effects are easy to see (success rate from 0 to 1). The hardware description is the paper's own account of the device used.
cum-annealing-tts-definition: Section VII C 1, equation (29), p.50: the paper defines TTS as Tcycle times log(1 - 0.99) over log(1 - Psol), and notes readout and reset make Tcycle not fixed.
cum-reverse-annealing-mechanism: Section VII C 2, p.52: the paper describes the reverse anneal procedure it uses (seed state, reverse toward the equal superposition Hamiltonian, pause, forward anneal).
cum-appendix-qubo-to-ising: Appendix A 1, p.59: the paper states the mapping z = 1 - 2s it uses between QUBO and Ising values.
cum-appendix-spsa-parameters: Appendix A 4, p.60 to p.61: the gradient from two evaluations at plus or minus epsilon, SPSA random parameter choice, Noisyopt default decay with alpha = 0.602 and gamma = 0.101, user-supplied a, c and niter.
cum-appendix-methods-hardware-software: Appendix A 5, p.62: Pyquil and Qiskit simulators checked for equal results, D-Wave Ocean for the classical solvers, Intel i7 and i5 desktops and laptops.
ambulance-gate-simulator-scope: Section VIII A, p.53: 'both quantum gate based methods (mainly using a simulator) and quantum annealing (using a live system)'. The paper's own statement of what it covered.

theory_low.qgrand-correct-iff-n-greater-k-plus-entr: Section V-A, equation (10), p.6: taken from [47, sec. 24.6.3] (Wilde) and the hashing bound; the paper gives only a set-counting remark, no proof. The paper says it holds for large n.
theory_low.qgrand-p-all-correctable-vs-almost-all: Section V-B, equations (13) to (16), p.7: the derivation uses a Taylor approximation (the approximate-equality and approximately-greater-than signs), and the 'P(f > 1 - epsilon) about 1' remark is asserted, not derived. It is for the ideal random-syndrome model, not the QRLC. An informal bound, not a proved result.
theory_low.qgrand-syndrome-strings-equally-distribu: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section V-B, p.7 gives one clause ('due to the linearity of the code') for the equal spread of the 4 to the n Pauli strings over the syndromes. The coset-size argument is not written out in the paper.
theory_low.qgrand-degenerate-probability-1-over-L: Section V-B, p.7: 'is ~ 1/L' is an estimate with no derivation. Section VII, p.12 only disregards degeneracy for moderate or high k.
theory_low.qgrand-bernoulli-weight-t-uncorrectable-: Section V-B1, p.7: an argument in prose that lower-weight patterns are always more likely. It disregards degeneracy as 'negligible for large k' and gives no proof; equation (23) is approximate (S much greater than 1).
theory_low.qgrand-membership-test-average-two-stabi: Section VI-A, equations (26) and (27), p.9: the sum is shown, but p = 1/2 per stabilizer and independence rest on the assumption that the encoding and stabilizers are random. The paper does not prove that its QRLCs meet that assumption (Section V-C shows they need enough gates). The value's 'because random' is a premise, not shown.
theory_low.qgrand-total-stabilizer-measurements-bou: Section VI-A, equation (29), p.9: the bound follows from the per-iteration average under 2, which rests on the same random-stabilizer assumption (p = 1/2, independence). The step from per-iteration cost to the total is only sketched. Not a proved result.
theory_low.qgrand-failure-modes-without-and-with-ab: Section VI-A, p.9 to p.10: a prose argument from the decoding rule, with no proof. 'Solely' also depends on noiseless gates and on disregarding degeneracy, which the paper only argues are negligible.
theory_low.qgrand-syndrome-decoding-storage-and-mea: Section VI-B, p.10: average-case counts (log2 NP bits, 2 NP bits, log2(N+1) measurements) rest on the random nature of the code. No derivation or proof in the paper.
theory_low.qgrand-stabilizer-ordering-negligible-sa: Section VI-C, p.10: 'it can be shown' with a pointer to Appendix A. Appendix A is an approximate derivation (binomial to normal, independence assumed, 'not exact') plus a numerical check in Fig. 9. Not a proof.
theory_low.qgrand-fidelity-lower-bound-by-bler: coordinator sign-off: the paper's text says 1 - Fmin is lower bounded by BLER, while its equation (32) gives the opposite direction, so the paper does not settle which holds; the reviewer's reason for HIGH was: Section VII, equations (31) and (32), p.11: the paper derives the bound from the stated worst case (every non-identity error gives F = 0): average fidelity at least the summed probability of non-degenerate correctable patterns, equal to 1 minus BLER. The derivation is in the paper. Note the text says '1 - Fmin is lower bounded by BLER', but equation (32) gives 1 - Fmin at most BLER, which is what the value says.
theory_low.qgrand-appendix-a-random-order-log2-N: Appendix A, p.13: average-case counts for random ordering stated with '~' and no derivation.
theory_low.qgrand-appendix-a-greedy-ordering-iterat: Appendix A, equation (35), p.13: an approximate derivation (binomial to normal, independent stabilizers, Jensen bound, large N and s) that the authors call 'not exact' and 'a rule of thumb'. Fig. 9 is a numerical fit. Not a proof.
theory_low.cum-expected-monotone-in-p: Section VI B 2, p.15: the authors say 'we expect' P(p+1) >= P(p) because the angles can be set to zero. That is an expectation, not a proof; the classical optimiser need not find the improvement (the paper itself later notes non-monotonic results).
theory_low.cum-3xy-search-space-1120: Section VI C 2, p.25: the count 4 x 4 x 70 = 1120 and the factor of about 60 are simple counting. But 'this advantage scales exponentially with the number of qubits in a given XY ring mixer' is asserted with no derivation (the paper cites [44] elsewhere), and the count assumes the mixers keep Hamming weight (cited, not proved here). Two claims, graded by the weaker.
